findings.description: The one-shot output-budget shrink on ProviderContextLimitError uses `continue` inside `for attempt in range(max_retries + 1)` and never sets `last_typed_error`. When the provider verdict arrives on the last permitted attempt (retry.max_retries: 0, or after transient failures consumed the budget), the loop simply ends: the shrunk request is never sent and the function raises RetriesExhaustedError('... unknown'). cheval has no ProviderContextLimitError to catch, so it treats the RetriesExhaustedError as walkable and sends the same oversize payload to the next hop, and no observed-bound row is written. This defeats the D-1.1b 'never walked' contract exactly in the configuration operators use to disable retries.
findings.failure_mode: Oversize payload is walked to every fallback hop (repeated provider 400s, wasted latency/cost), typed CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE exit and calibration record are lost; RetriesExhaustedError reports 'unknown' cause.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `last_typed_error = e` before `continue`, and perform the single shrink retry outside the attempt budget (e.g. `if attempt >= max_retries: raise` is wrong too — instead re-issue the shrunk request immediately in the except branch, or extend the loop by one iteration when the shrink is taken). Add a test with max_retries=0 asserting the shrunk request is sent and ProviderContextLimitError propagates if it fails again.

findings.description: `_ceiling_unverified` is computed once from the HEAD entry's pre-flight outcome and then consulted on every hop. Two consequences in the chain walk: (a) any RateLimitError on any hop ends the invocation as RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED while the flag is set, including a plain requests-per-minute 429 that says nothing about payload size, and including a 429 on a fallback hop whose bound is calibrated/verified; (b) a ProviderContextLimitError on a calibrated fallback is classed CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT. The head test file provided (test_ceiling_e2e.py: test_request_rate_429_while_unverified_walks_to_the_next_hop, test_unverified_status_is_per_hop_not_inherited_from_the_head) asserts the opposite behaviour, so as written the diff fails its own suite or the suite was not run against it.
findings.failure_mode: A transient request-rate 429 on a hop above the probed bound terminates the call with exit RATE_LIMITED and writes a spurious calibration row instead of walking to a healthy fallback; calibration rows mis-classify the catalog's error as 'unverified'.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the 429 short-circuit on `_e.token_limited` (or equivalent) AND on a per-hop unverified flag computed from this hop's own input_bound decision (estimate > hop's probed/calibrated bound), not the head's pre-flight flag. Derive the ProviderContextLimitError class from the same per-hop flag.

findings.description: The provider error text is copied verbatim into `models_failed[].message_redacted` (`str(_exc)`) and into the stderr `_error_json` message without passing through the redaction helper that the rest of the envelope path uses. Provider error bodies can echo request fragments; a secret-shaped string in that body lands in the MODELINV envelope and the operator log. The head test test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message asserts redaction and would fail against this code.
findings.failure_mode: Secret-shaped content from a provider 400/413 body is persisted unredacted in model-invoke.jsonl and printed to stderr, bypassing the audit chain's redaction guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `str(_exc)` through the existing redaction helper (the same one `redact_payload_strings` applies) before building the models_failed row and the `_error_json` message; keep the field name `message_redacted` truthful.

findings.description: The pre-flight may replace the heuristic estimate with the provider's authoritative count (`_walk_estimate = _preflight_outcome.estimate.tokens`). The per-hop I1 fit then shrinks `_hop_budget` from that count (max_tokens ≈ context_window − count), and `_lookup_max_input_tokens(..., max_tokens=_hop_budget)` yields a bound ≈ count. But the per-hop walk gate that follows (`if _input_threshold is not None: ... estimate_tokens(messages)`) compares the HEURISTIC estimate against that bound. Whenever the heuristic exceeds the count and I1 shrank, the comparison heuristic > (cw − (cw − count)) = count is true by construction, so the head hop is recorded as ROUTING_MISS and skipped even though the provider said the request fits.
findings.failure_mode: With a real Anthropic adapter (count_tokens available) and a prompt near the window, the head entry is deterministically walked past; the request lands on a fallback (or exits CHAIN_EXHAUSTED) despite the authoritative count having passed the gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `_walk_estimate` (the count when available) in the per-hop walk gate instead of recomputing `estimate_tokens(messages)`, or compute the I1 fit and the walk-gate comparison from the same estimate value.

findings.description: When LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_INPUT_GATE=1 (so `_walk_estimate` is None) and the provider message states no numbers, `_obs` becomes 0 and `record_observed(observed_input_tokens=0, provider_limit=None)` is still written to the store. Downstream readers that do not filter non-positive values (loa-status.sh's jq per reviewer item 7) render 'observed -1'.
findings.failure_mode: A zero observation row pollutes `.run/ceiling-observed.json` and produces a nonsensical status line; depending on the ceiling reducer it may also lower the bound to 0/−1.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the store write (but keep the envelope `calibration_needed`) when neither the provider nor the estimate yields a positive token count; or compute a fresh `estimate_tokens(messages)` for the record.

findings.description: The long-context premium triggers on `input_tokens > threshold` only, where `input_tokens` excludes cache_read/cache_creation tokens (they are separate Anthropic usage fields). The provider's published rule is on total input tokens for the request (including cached prompt). A request with 150K uncached + 100K cache-read tokens is 250K input and billed premium by the provider, but this code bills base rate while still applying the multipliers to cache traffic only when uncached input alone crosses 200K.
findings.failure_mode: Ledger under-reports cost for long cached prompts above the premium threshold; `long_context` flag and cost-report long_context_rows are wrong for those rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens` against the threshold (verify against the provider's billing rule and document the choice in the catalog `verified` flag).

findings.cross_file_justification: The default change propagates to every adapter and CLI path that reads request.temperature; only anthropic/bedrock/google/openai adapters are updated in the diff.
findings.description: `CompletionRequest.temperature` now defaults to None and cheval passes `binding.temperature` through unchanged. Only four adapters were updated to use `wire_temperature`. Any other consumer that writes `request.temperature` straight into a body or CLI flag (other HTTP adapters such as openrouter/deepseek-style, headless CLI adapters building `--temperature`, async/poll paths, dry-run printing, or code comparing `request.temperature != 0.7`) will now emit `temperature: null` or the string 'None'.
findings.failure_mode: Provider 400 ('temperature must be a number') or a CLI arg parse failure on hops not touched by this diff; the chain walks past them with PROVIDER_OUTAGE and the cause is obscured.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep for `request.temperature` / `.temperature` across loa_cheval/providers and the CLI adapters; route every wire write through `wire_temperature` and add an adapter-matrix test that asserts no body contains a null temperature.

findings.description: The new probe returns False for any `GET /models` status other than 200 or 404. Proxies/gateways that front the Messages API but answer 401/403/405 on `/models` (common with key-scoped gateways) now report the provider unhealthy even though `/messages` works, whereas the previous probe exercised the actual messages path.
findings.failure_mode: loa-status / health gating reports Anthropic down behind such a gateway; operators may disable a working provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Fall through to the one-token message probe for any non-200 on `/models` except an explicit auth failure that the messages path would share (401 with an Anthropic error envelope), or make the models-endpoint step best-effort only.
